text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Schleswig-Holstein state wants to legalise sale of cannabis
- Constitutional court opens hearing on electoral law
- Palestinian sentenced to 12 years for 1977 hijacking
- Study says courts are too rigorous in protecting employees against dismissal
- Deutsche Telekom shares fall as speculators take profits
HANDELSBLATT
- Interior Minister Kanther plans new measures against organised crime as big case of money laundering uncovered
- Deutsche Telekom shares fall as speculators take profits
- Savings banks plan to pull out of agreement on bank fees
- German President Herzog discusses human rights with Chinese President Jiang Zemin
- Bundesbank sees companies making higher profits this year
- Prosecutors bring charges over East German ship orders
- Siemens and Motorola have no comment on report of joint 12-inch wafer manufacturing project
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Federal Labour Office needs five billion marks more in 1997 than government has provided for in budget
- Bonn takes steps to protect its nationals in Iran
- Palestinian sentenced to 12 years for 1977 hijacking
- Court rules rejected asylum seekers cannot be deported if civil war going on in homeland
- Bundesbank warns against window-dressing financial data in the interests of monetary union
- Deutsche Telekom shares fall as speculators take profits
- Bundesbank to stick with fixed-rate tenders
- Car production and exports rise strongly
- Bundesbank says company profits to be up again in 1996
DIE WELT
- Interior Minister Kanther wants to get tougher on organised crime
- German President Herzog discusses human rights in China
- Bundesbank says company profits to be up again in 1996
- Pension fund association rejects Finance Minister Waigel's suggestion that pensions should be fully taxed
- Western Germans less keen to go on health cures
